/-!
# Written on the Wall II - Conjecture 63

*Reference:*
[E. DeLaVina, Written on the Wall II, Conjectures of Graffiti.pc](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)

## Counterexample

The conjecture is false for the lexicographic product $C_5[K_4]$. This graph
has minimum even-distance count $9$, while its largest induced forest and
largest induced bipartite subgraph both have order $4$. The conjectured lower
bound is therefore $\lceil(9 + 4 + 1)/3\rceil = 5 > 4$.
-/

@[expose] public section

namespace WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture63

open SimpleGraph

/--
WOWII [Conjecture 63](http://cms.dt.uh.edu/faculty/delavinae/research/wowII/)
asked whether every simple connected graph $G$ satisfies
$f(G) \geq \lceil(\min_v \operatorname{distEven}(v) + b(G) + 1)/3\rceil$.
The answer is no, as witnessed by $C_5[K_4]$.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 5, formal_proof using lean4 at
"https://github.com/Kuberwastaken/wowii-63-85-counterexample/blob/cba739842ec59adf7426c180009175b31935701d/lean/WOWII63.lean#L184-L195"]
theorem conjecture63 : answer(False) ↔
    ∀ (α : Type) [Fintype α] [DecidableEq α] [Nontrivial α]
      (G : SimpleGraph α) (_h : G.Connected),
      let minDistEven := (Finset.univ.image (G.distEven ·)).min' (by simp)
      ⌈((minDistEven : ℝ) + G.b + 1) / 3⌉ ≤ (G.largestInducedForestSize : ℝ) := by
  sorry

/-- Every vertex is counted among the vertices at even distance from itself. -/
@[category test, AMS 5]
example (G : SimpleGraph (Fin 3)) (v : Fin 3) : 0 < G.distEven v := by
  unfold SimpleGraph.distEven
  apply Finset.card_pos.mpr
  exact ⟨v, Finset.mem_filter.mpr
    ⟨Finset.mem_univ _, ⟨0, by simp [SimpleGraph.dist_self]⟩⟩⟩

end WrittenOnTheWallII.GraphConjecture63

reformulations.difference: Lean adds [Nontrivial α], whereas the source simply quantifies over simple connected graphs, without explicitly excluding the one-vertex graph.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: The only omitted connected graph is the one-vertex graph. Its minimum even-distance count, largest induced bipartite subgraph order, and largest induced forest order are all 1. Hence the inequality becomes ceil((1 + 1 + 1)/3) ≤ 1, which holds. Empty graphs are excluded by connectedness. Consequently adding or removing Nontrivial leaves the universal proposition, and therefore its negative-answer formulation, unchanged. The equivalence is proved as Review63.nontrivial_restriction_iff in /workspace/review/scratch.lean, without sorryAx.

review.notes: Both the main theorem and the proved test match the source definitions. In particular, distance zero is even, so counting the vertex itself is correct. Connectedness excludes the distance function's unreachable-pair default. Scratch Lean checks established that the two suprema are over nonempty bounded sets and attain the stated maxima, and tested the empty, singleton, and smallest permitted connected cases. The cited counterexample proof compiled against this checkout's definitions after changing its import; it verifies minimum even-distance count 9 and both induced-subgraph maxima 4, giving the contradiction 5 ≤ 4. Its axiom report contains no sorryAx, but does contain the generated native_decide axioms. Thus answer(False), research solved, and the external formal_proof record are supported. The archived source's older O label is not a reason to revert the verified solved status.
